headline: Residents spoke at public hearing on planBTV New North End; council to act December 7th.
summary: Planning staff said the plan sets a long-term vision for the New North End over the next two decades and does not approve any project, zoning change, or funding. Some speakers backed the plan, while others asked for more time, better outreach, and a guarantee that parks stay parks. The council also approved a housing infrastructure agreement with Watershed A LLC for SECORD Phase 1, where the developer estimates $12.2 million in eligible costs. A driveway and curb cut license at 15 Ward Street was denied.
decisions: Approved the council consent agenda, unanimously.
Approved 2026-2027 first and third-class liquor licenses for Main Street HQ, 198 Main Street, with conditions, unanimously.
Ratified the appointment of assistant election officials for the November 2026 general election, unanimously.
Approved the Housing Infrastructure Agreement with Watershed A LLC for SECORD Phase 1, unanimously.
Approved a resolution supporting graduate student workers at the University of Vermont, 9 to 2, with 1 absent.
Failed: motion to refer the 15 Ward Street driveway and curb cut request to the License Committee, 2 to 9, with 1 absent.
Denied the driveway and curb cut license for 15 Ward Street, 9 to 2, with 1 absent.
discussion: planBTV New North End plan: Public speakers split on the plan. Some said residents learned of it too late and asked for more time, while others backed it and wanted parks kept free of housing.

SECORD Phase 1 financing: Council members asked how the tax increment would work. The developer said the state CHIP program would cover about 42% of $12.2 million in eligible infrastructure, and that an application would go to VEPC in December.
Graduate worker contract: Speakers described long bargaining and the cost of living for graduate students. Some council members said the council should not weigh in on collective bargaining.

15 Ward Street parking: Speakers said the spot is needed for tenants who work night shifts. DPW said the greenbelt parking is not warranted and that the 2021 approval for five years had no renewal clause.
Problem properties: Staff reported on vacant and distressed buildings. The permitting department projected about $90,000 in vacant building fees this fiscal year, above the $20,000 budgeted.
